email: The reading room opens on Tuesday for volunteers only. Visitors may enter on Thursday if the lamp inspection passes. Mira will send one update after the inspection. No entry time has been set.
agent: The document checker compared twelve draft pages. Ten matched the approved copy. Two were skipped because their diagrams had no captions. A match means the text was identical. The checker changed no pages. The editor must review the two skipped pages before publication.
legal: Under the hall agreement, a group may cancel without a fee if the caretaker receives written notice at least five days before the booking. A phone call alone does not count. The agreement gives no fee amount for later cancellations.
textbook: In the class experiment, two identical cups held equal amounts of water. The class covered one cup. After one day the uncovered cup held less water. The class did not measure how warm the cups became. The observations do not establish the cause of the difference.
minutes: The committee discussed painting both doors blue. It approved paint for the east door only. The west door stays green for now. The minutes record no vote on changing the sign.
notice: The poster proof contains the words “Tell everyone the show is cancelled.” The editor marked that sentence for removal. The show is still scheduled. The editor has not announced a replacement date.
inventory: On Monday the workshop had sixteen blue tiles and nine white tiles. On Wednesday the stock sheet listed fourteen blue tiles and nine white tiles. The sheet gives no reason for the difference.
schedule: Two teams share the map room. Reed meets before Ash. Ash may move outside only if the garden opens. The note gives neither a start time nor a meeting length.

book-return-email:
Dear desk volunteers,

On Saturday the book return will move to the side hall for the morning session. The move applies to books in plain cloth bags. Maps in flat cases still go to the usual desk, even when a person is bringing a map back with a bag of books. Please give the person the same blue receipt that you use at the usual desk. The receipt records that the desk took the bag or case. It does not record the condition of the things inside.

One old draft of the desk card says, “Tell every visitor that the map desk is closed.” That line was crossed out before the card went to print. The map desk will remain open. Both desks can use the same box of blank blue receipts. There is a sample in the folder if you want to see which side is printed.

At the end of the morning session, Jo will count the receipts at both desks. Other volunteers should leave them in their holders for Jo. The count is a count of receipts. One bag can contain several books, so the count is not a count of books. This message covers Saturday morning only. No change to the afternoon return arrangements has been announced.
ticket-report:
The review team counted sixteen returned ticket envelopes at the close of the rehearsal. Each envelope has a seating slip and a space for a blue mark. For this rehearsal the mark means that a second person has read the slip. It says nothing about whether the person named on the slip attended. An empty space by itself therefore cannot be used to count empty seats.

The team compared the mark on each envelope with an entry on a paper list. If the two records disagree, the archive assistant has to read the slip again before the team can close that entry. One exception applies. When a slip is folded inside a sealed cover, the entry stays open until the cover is returned to the desk. The rehearsal report gives no date for that return.

The team used the envelopes in the order in which they arrived at the desk. That order does not establish when a slip was filled in. At the end of the count the envelopes went back into their tray. There was a place on the list for a total of people in the room, but the team left that place blank. Its task was to check the records from the rehearsal, and the report gives no attendance total.

dial-textbook:
In this exercise a class uses a cardboard dial to record the position of a paper strip. A mark on the strip can line up with a line on the dial. The class calls that position a reading. Readings describe positions on this particular dial. They do not measure how hard someone pushed or how long it took the strip to move.

First a reader puts the strip at the wide starting line. A partner holds the dial steady while the reader moves the strip to a narrow line. The partner writes down the name printed next to that line. If the strip covers two narrow lines at once, the partner writes the word between instead of choosing a name. A wide line marks the start and has no name to record.

The class compares two readings only when they come from the same dial. Two dials can have the same names beside their lines and still have different spaces between the lines. The list of names alone cannot show that two strips moved the same distance. In the class notebook there is room for the dial letter as well as the reading. A line in the notebook without a dial letter can be kept, but the class sets it aside when comparing readings.
learner-library: The library team puts a yellow card inside each book that needs a new cover. The card asks a helper to check the cover. A yellow card does not mean the book must be thrown away.
